title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Written Notice of Loss
content:
Written notice of loss is how a claim under `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims` comes into being. The claimant gives the notice in person; the desk does not give it for the claimant.

## What the notice carries

A notice records the container where the loss arose, its kind, whether it could be seen at delivery, the packages and weight affected, and an amount. Everything except the amount is entered exactly as the claimant states it. The amount entered measures what is exposed in the named container, on the line's basis for notices. The proven loss is a different figure, established only at settlement; the claimant quantifies its loss separately, in the claim documents that follow.

## Capability of the tool

`lodge_cargo_claim_268664bf` is the means by which a claimant puts its own written notice of a loss on record. A call opens a fresh claim file on the cover for the container named, holding the kind of loss, whether it was visible at delivery, the amount entered, and the packages and weight affected. The notice bears today's date; the new file begins at the notice-registered stage, `notice_registered`, and the cover moves to `claim_open`. The claimant receives a claim reference to use in all later contact.

## Invocation

This tool belongs to the customer. The agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it to lodge the notice; the agent does not run it on the customer's behalf.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `cover_id` | the cargo cover under which the notice is given, as the desk passes it on from the cover lookup | identifier |
| `customer_id` | the claimant giving the notice, as the desk passes it on from the customer profile lookup | identifier |
| `container_number` | the container in which the loss arose | ISO 6346, four letters then seven digits, no spaces, for example AHLU5123450 |
| `damage_type` | the nature of the loss | one value from the list below |
| `damage_apparent_at_delivery` | whether the loss could be seen at delivery | true where the loss was visible at delivery and noted on the delivery receipt; false where it came to light only afterwards |
| `claimed_amount_usd` | the amount entered on the notice as the loss claimed | US dollars, zero or more, two decimals; kept rounded half-to-even |
| `affected_package_count` | how many packages were lost or damaged | whole packages |
| `affected_weight_kg` | gross weight of the lost or damaged goods | kilograms to one decimal place; kept rounded to one decimal |

Values accepted for `damage_type`: `physical_damage`, goods broken, crushed or harmed in some other physical way; `wet_damage`, goods spoiled by water or moisture; `temperature_damage`, perishable goods harmed by the temperature at which they were carried, such as cargo that thawed or warmed; `contamination`, goods that became contaminated or tainted; `shortage`, packages absent from the container; `total_loss`, all the goods in the container lost; `delay_loss`, a financial loss caused by undamaged goods arriving late.

## Return

On success the tool reports `status` "lodged", the new claim reference as `claim_id`, the `cover_id`, the `notice_date` on which the notice reached the line (YYYY-MM-DD), an `outcome` reading `notice_registered`, and a `cover_status` reading `claim_open`.
